text:
Elaine (Sales): Hey team, ACME asked to scale back their Dedicated POC burst window and temporarily reduce reserved headroom to save costs next week. POC pool id: ded-poc-acme-03. Current burst window 2h, requested 30m. Guaranteed headroom 20 -> want 6. Also they want hosted API key rotation for the demo. Can we do this without violating SLA? Need confirmation by EOD Thu.

Mike (Eng): Quick clarifying q's — is a big traffic spike still expected during the demo or just baseline traffic after the demo? Do they need canary/baseline fallback to hosted? Any strict min_capacity constraints from procurement?

Irene (ACME): After the demo traffic will drop to ~10% of peak for 72hrs. We only need the higher capacity during the live demo (tomorrow). No canary needed, but we want fast rollback if something spikes. Also: are there any penalties for short-term headroom reductions?

Charlie (Infra): We can do a temporary headroom reduction + shorten burst window, but a few notes: 1) Reservation contract enforces a 24h change lead for committed capacity changes on Dedicated pools — we can apply a temporary "ephemeral headroom" workaround for short windows if Sales signs off on billing exposure. 2) Burst window = 30m is fine; autoscaler cooldown should be tightened to avoid thrash. 3) Hosted fallback (small model) must be configured as a fallback route. 4) For API key rotation: create an ephemeral key with TTL and restrict to pool + IP range.

ops-bot: [automated] Provisioning change request received for ded-poc-acme-03. Ticket #POC-5821 created. Current status: pending-approval.

Mike (Eng): Proposed config changes (apply to pool ded-poc-acme-03):
```json
{"min_capacity":"6","burst_window":"30m","cooldown":"15m","fallback_route":"hosted-small","temp_burst_credits":"50"}
```
Notes: - cooldown 15m to reduce oscillation - temp_burst_credits 50 are ephemeral credits for the demo window only (will auto-expire) - set alerting: >80% usage for 5m -> page on-call.

Charlie (Infra): Implementation plan:
1) Sales approves billing exposure for ephemeral credits.
2) I’ll schedule the ephemeral headroom change for T-2h before demo. Ops will apply the pool patch and attach a temporary quota.
3) Rotate API key: create ephemeral key name `acme-poc-demo-ephemeral` TTL 72h, restrict to Redwood Hosted and ded-poc-acme-03 IPs.
4) Configure fallback in routing policy to hosted-small with automatic model swap at 300ms tail latency.
Estimated timeline: 90 minutes ops work, change window T-2h.

Elaine (Sales): Approved. Sales signs off on ephemeral credits for the demo window only. Please proceed — Irene, confirm you’re OK with API key TTL=72h and IP restrictions?

Irene (ACME): Confirmed. TTL 72h and IP allowlist is fine. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Mike (Eng): I’ll open a short runbook for on-call during the demo: include rollback command and how to revert headroom. Snippet for rollback:
```bash
# revert headroom
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.ai/dedicated/pools/ded-poc-acme-03 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"min_capacity":20,"burst_window":"2h","cooldown":"30m"}'
```

Charlie (Infra): Ticket PO C-5821 updated with timeline + runbook. I’ll apply changes at T-2h and post updates here.

ops-bot: [automated] PO C-5821 status -> scheduled. Change window: 2026-04-02T14:00Z -> 2026-04-02T16:00Z.

Elaine (Sales): Thanks all — I’ll notify ACME and confirm the demo schedule. :thumbsup:

Irene (ACME): Thanks team! Excited for tomorrow.
